research_rationale:
Executive Order 13687 (Imposing Additional Sanctions With Respect To North Korea; 80 FR 819) is held in the Federal Register print (FR Doc. 2015-00058) and was read in full. The inventory as frozen has 23 clauses (an opening clause consisting only of the words 'I hereby order:' and sections 1 to 9 with their paragraphs). The preamble sentence in which the President finds a continuing threat and 'hereby expand[s] the scope of the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13466' is an operative act that the frozen opening clause omits, so the opening clause is corrected to span the whole preamble from the President's findings through 'I hereby order:'. The order has no sunset or terminating condition of its own. A sentence-by-sentence search of the held texts that print the number 13687 (the Federal Register print, continuation notices, other Federal Register documents and CFR text) for revocation, supersession, rescission, termination, amendment or repeal language next to the number found none. The Federal Register catalog search (later-events:ofr_catalog) returned only cross-references to this order from North Korea notices and related orders. The other general instrument in the packet, Executive Order 14294 of May 9, 2025 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations), does not print this number and states a prosecution policy for criminal regulatory offenses, which gives no reason to treat any clause as extinguished. Executive Order 13687 itself relies on the emergency declared in Executive Order 13466, so the held notices continuing that emergency (each of which names Executive Order 13687) are the continuation predicate. The later North Korea order held in the packet (Executive Order 13810) names this order among those under which property is blocked and does not revoke, supersede or amend it. Because the order depends on a declared emergency, the 12 annual continuation notices held for it are attached to every clause; the last, the Notice of June 22, 2026, continues the emergency beyond June 26, 2026, which covers 2026-10-14. Every clause is operative on that date.
